newsitem.title: USA: Senator to offer bill to boost airwave sales.
newsitem.headline: Senator to offer bill to boost airwave sales.

text.p: A bill to maximize the money the government raises from the sale of the nation's airwaves will be introduced next week, a key lawmaker said Thursday.
"There's got to be some appreciation for the market," Sen. John McCain, an Arizona Republican, told a news conference.

The Commerce Committee chairman noted the problems that wireless phone carriers are experiencing on Wall Street. The recent drop in the value of spectrum sold by the government has made it tougher for the carriers to raise money from investors.

Critics of the current airwave-sales policy charge that the government is selling off too much spectrum over too short a period of time, driving down its price and the amount of money the government can fetch from airwave auctions.
Among other things, McCain's spectrum legislation would make it easier for the Commerce Department to pinpoint what airwaves slices could be sold.
It also would slap a "reasonable" time limit on the Federal Communication Commission's allocation of spectrum.
And to prevent spectrum from being dumped on the market, the bill would allow for a "reasonable time lag" between the allocation of the spectrum and its auction by the FCC.
Reflecting current problems, the No. 2 bidder at the government's high-flying wireless phone auction last year filed for bankruptcy protection from its creditors earlier this month.

The problems facing Pocket Communictions Inc. and several other top bidders at the $10.2 billion dollar sale have raised doubts about whether the FCC will ever collect all the money it is owed for the spectrum.
Separately, McCain also said he was considering crafting into legislation the FCC's recent rules giving broadcasters free licenses to provide high-definition digital television.
Under the FCC's rules, broadcasters must return their existing analogue licenses to the government by the year 2006. The government is expected to auction those licenses for other uses.
